messages:
sara-partnerships: Heads-up — Solara (customer) is blocked on the private deployment checklist. SI partner (PartnerSys) says the image boots but services time out. Need an architecture review + short triage today. @anya-arch @miguel-se

anya-arch: ok — can you drop the diagram they used? rough questions: is the NLB internet-facing or internal? are we using host vs target-group health checks? what ports are expected by the image?

miguel-se: PartnerSys confirms it's an internal NLB, but their Terraform set the target group health check to /health (HTTP) on port 80 while our runtime expects gRPC on 50051. mismatch. They also locked the firewall to internal-only CIDR. quick reproduce steps from the SI: 
```
# PartnerSys snippet (sanitized)
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "tg" {
  port     = 80
  protocol = "HTTP"
  path     = "/health"
}
```
They say changing to TCP 50051 caused connections to succeed locally.

rupert-devops: saw NLB health check flapping to 502 from our side too. logs show our runtime returning 200 only on /ready but not on /health. Also, SSM session to the instance shows iptables blocking outbound to our KV cache endpoint (10.2.4.11:443). suspect security group/inbound rules are overly restrictive.

olivia-cs: customer pushed for EOW go/no-go; they'd like a mitigation path so their product demo isn't blocked. can we offer a short-term hosted fallback? they prefer private but will accept hosted for demo.

deploy-bot: [build-status] private-image: build/registry push succeeded, but image-signing hook flagged missing attestations for marketplace, details in CI. See https://ci.redwood/integrations/2345

sara-partnerships: thanks — two asks: (1) quick arch review + exact change list we give PartnerSys, (2) a mitigation plan to keep the demo alive (hosted fallback or routing canary). can we do a 30m call 1630 PT? :hourglass_flowing_sand: @rupert-devops @anya-arch

anya-arch: proposed immediate remediation:
- update target group to TCP 50051, health check path -> use TCP health check
- open outbound 443 to KV cache 10.2.4.11 (or point to regional cache endpoint)
- change NLB to internal + attach Cloud NAT for egress if they need internet egress from private subnets
Command we can ask PartnerSys to run:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn tg-abc --protocol TCP --port 50051 --health-check-protocol TCP
# and update SG: allow egress 443 to 10.2.4.11
```
This preserves private footprint and fixes runtime expectations quickly.

miguel-se: i'll prep a short checklist and a one-page diff for PartnerSys with the exact Terraform snippets they need. Also can configure a temporary routing policy that sends 10% of traffic to Redwood hosted model (fallback) if we detect >5% failures. That buys breathing room for the demo.

rupert-devops: i'll open incident ticket INC-2065 and assign SRE on-call to monitor NLB healthchecks and the KV cache egress. i'll also attach the packet captures and the 502 logs.

olivia-cs: confirming with Solara — they accepted the 1630 PT slot. i'll send calendar invite and include PartnerSys leads. thanks all.

sara-partnerships: great — meet at 1630. Miguel/Anya please bring the Terraform snippets and a rollback/fallback playbook. :thumbsup:
